newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks finish lower after U.S. jobs report.
newsitem.headline: French stocks finish lower after U.S. jobs report.

text.p: French stocks finished lower on Friday after a robust U.S. jobs report hurt Wall Street stocks by fanning concerns about the outlook for U.S. interest rates.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index closed down 21.58 points, or 0.92 percent, at 2,327.50, while the CAC-40 futures contract fell 20 points to 2,331. Volume was a heavy eight billion francs.

The poor performance of the Tokyo market, which ended the week at a two-year low after a string of losses, had also unnerved the bourse, but investors said the driving force remains the U.S. market. They said investors will be waiting to see U.S. consumer inflation data due on Tuesday.
The U.S. jobs report showed the United States added 262,000 new jobs in December, far above the consensus estimate of 192,000. The unemployment rate was unchanged at 5.3 percent.
Despite Friday's fall, the bourse's CAC index ended the week with a 1.90 percent gain.
Recurring speculation about a restructuring of the French pharmaceutical industry enlivened trading on the bourse.
* Shares in Elf-Aquitaine's drugs subsidiary Sanofi rallied 6.17 percent to 568 francs on rumours of a deal with Synthelabo, majority-controlled by L'Oreal.
Synthelabo denied the rumour. L'Oreal declined comment.
The sector is rife with speculation following a number of mergers, and Sanofi's stock has become closely watched since Elf recently said that it would be willing to give up control.
* Via Banque, a unit of Paribas, rallied 8.43 percent to 193 francs on rumours that it may be the next Paribas asset up for sale.
The financial group said on Thursday that it would sell bank Credit du Nord to Societe Generale. Paribas' stock eased 0.31 percent to 353.10 francs after rocketing 4.02 percent on Thursday.
* Accor shares rose 0.15 percent against the trend, closing at 656 francs, after its 50-50 Europcar venture with Volkswagen reported an operating profit for 1996.
* Renault shares initially shot up one percent to 112.40 francs on reports that the company was scrambling to boost production of the Megane Scenic to meet huge demand.
But profit-taking by investors seeking to reduce their holdings in Renault because of its poor earnings prospects crushed the rally. The stock closed down 2.34 percent at 108.50 francs.
